people.notes: PLACEHOLDER: working-to-62 figure comes from your SSA statement (ssa.gov/myaccount). The stopping-now figure (2600) is a placeholder — get the real $0-future-earnings estimate from ssa.gov's estimator with average future annual salary set to $0.

people.name: Jordan
people.notes: EXAMPLE SETUP: this person is modelled with no earnings record of their own — under 40 credits, so own benefit is 0 and only the spousal benefit applies. That is a configuration, not an assumption about you: set hasOwnBenefit=true and both PIA figures from the SSA statement if this person has a work record.

accounts.name: 401(k) — current employer
accounts.notes: PLACEHOLDER balance and allocation. Shaped like a 2035 target-date fund — roughly 68/32 stocks/bonds today, which the engine glides toward the target year automatically. Set targetDateFund.targetYear (or delete it and set a fixed allocation) to match what this account actually holds. Rolled into the traditional IRA at separation in every scenario.

accounts.name: Taxable brokerage
accounts.notes: PLACEHOLDER. Together with savings this is the liquid money available before 59 1/2 — the bridge the 72(t) and rule-of-55 logic exist to supplement.

accounts.name: Savings
accounts.notes: PLACEHOLDER. High-yield savings; earns the T-bill return as taxable interest.

health.notes: PLACEHOLDER: acaBenchmarkMonthly (1480) is an ILLUSTRATIVE full-price household premium for the second-lowest-cost Silver plan covering two people in their early fifties in a low-cost inland county — the right order of magnitude, and nothing more. This number drives the premium tax credit and the 400%-FPL cliff, so it is the single most valuable field to replace: get the real one from healthcare.gov (or your state marketplace) by pricing a Silver plan for your ages and ZIP, and set acaQuoteYear to the year you priced. employerPremiumShareMonthly 200 is a PLACEHOLDER too — set your real per-month payroll deduction.
